items.title: They are literally "Decision" models!!! The threat was in the name the whole time.
items.pt:
Watch a junior developer learn in 2019, then watch one in 2026.


2019: they guess. They break staging. They feel it in their stomach. They learn and never break it that way again.
2026: they ask. It answers. Staging is fine. And nothing was learned, but data was gone. TO a third party. For free.


Same job title and pay band. A completely different amount of human being at the end of it.


  
  
  The name was the tell


We call them decision models now. Not writing models. Not search models. D

items.title: Proving Your Tech Work Experience: An Express Entry Evidence Checklist
items.pt:
A developer's job title rarely tells the whole story. The same title can describe application development, infrastructure operations, technical sales or a mix of responsibilities. For an Express Entry application, a useful employment file connects the work claimed in the application with reliable evidence of what actually happened.

This checklist focuses on organizing evidence. It does not determine whether a particular job qualifies or how many points an applicant should receive.

items.title: Mississippi Has No Mini-WARN Law — Federal WARN Is the Only Notice Workers Get
items.pt:
Mississippi workers facing a mass layoff get exactly one layer of legal protection: the federal WARN Act. The state has no mini-WARN law of its own, no lower threshold, no longer notice period, no state penalty for short notice. That was confirmed in a review of official sources as of July 24, 2026. If your employer or the layoff is too small for federal WARN, Mississippi law requires no advance notice at all.

items.title: $Z$-sight: Unifying Vision-Language-Action and Latent World Modeling
items.pt: We introduce $Z$-sight, a unified robot foundation model that couples vision-language-action (VLA) and generative latent world modeling. Video-based world action models (WAMs) show the value of joint future-and-action generation for control, yet inherit the heavy cost of video generators. items.title: Jailbreak Detection on Large Language Models via Contrastive Prototype Structures
items.pt: Jailbreak attempts and harmful prompts remain a challenge for the safe deployment of large language models. We study whether contrastively learned representations can support safety detection without training an additional downstream classifier. We propose Jailbreak Detection with Prototype Inference (JDPI), which uses binary safety labels to construct harmful and benign prototypes and makes predictions from relative prototype distances. JDPI uses only binary safety labels for encoder adaptation

items.title: Mapping the AI Supply Chain: Dependencies, Vulnerabilities, and Market Concentration in the AI Ecosystem
items.pt: AI systems are built across many organizations that contribute models, data, compute, capital, talent, and other assets. While the layers of the AI stack are relatively well understood, the relationships between actors and components across layers remains sparsely documented.
